observation.visible_scene: A beach at sunset viewed toward the ocean horizon. The sky fills the upper half with layered clouds lit in orange, gold and teal, the sun a bright orange glow sitting just above the horizon slightly right of center. A band of breaking white-foam waves crosses the mid-frame ocean, and a wide flat wet-sand foreground mirrors the sky in gold (left) and blue-green (right), with a thin curved water edge on the right side of the sand.
visible_changes: The white foam line of the breaking waves shifts and re-textures continuously across the ocean band, indicating an ongoing wave/swash motion rather than a single event.
The thin sheet of water and its curved edge on the right foreground advance and recede slightly, changing the boundary between water and bare wet sand.
The shimmering reflections on the wet sand change brightness and pattern as the water film moves.
The horizon, sun position, and overall cloud shapes remain in the same place from first to last frame, indicating a static camera and essentially still sky.
outside_clip_unknowns: The wave cycle is already in progress at the start and continues past the end; no onset or completion of any wave is shown.
Whether the clouds drift at all over longer time is not determinable from this short excerpt.
uncertain_details: The exact direction and magnitude of the swash on the foreground sand is subtle and partly ambiguous between frames.
Any very slow cloud motion is below the resolution of change visible between consecutive samples.
